speaker: Sheila Dikshit
venue: Public rally in Delhi and other venues during 2013
quote_english: The power tariff in Delhi is much lower than that in other metropolitan cities and even other cities and towns in the National Capital Region.
summary: Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit said Delhi's power tariffs were the lowest among cities; a Mint claim check citing a Deloitte analysis found that in 2013 only Maharashtra, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh had higher retail tariffs than Delhi.

govt_response.title: Claim Check: Sheila Dikshit on Delhi's power tariffs - Mint
govt_response.summary: Mint found Dikshit was wrong that Delhi's tariffs were the lowest among cities, but right that the Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission, not the government, decides tariffs.

analysis:
Dikshit made the tariff claim at multiple venues in 2013, including a rally on 1 December, according to Mint's claim check. She also said tariffs could not be changed or amended by the government.

Mint's analysis, based on a Deloitte comparison of 2013 retail tariffs for a 300 kWh monthly consumption on a 4 kW connection, found that only Maharashtra, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh had higher tariffs than Delhi. It concluded she was wrong on the 'lowest tariffs' point but right that the DERC sets tariffs.

The claim that Delhi's tariffs were the lowest among cities is not supported by the tariff comparison, though the procedural point about the regulator was correct.
